answer: An operator copying one text across 132 aliases therefore pays for 132 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, as the hash is the same for all of them. Since the whisper hash is stored at intake, the cipher graph groups the endorsements and the ocean audit reveals the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 8 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
